requirement_text: The system shall ingest candidate resumes, cover letters, and application form responses submitted through the recruitment portal.

assessment.summary: FR-1 ingests untrusted candidate-supplied documents with no input specification, integrity or validation controls. Malformed or manipulated inputs could degrade accuracy and cause unfair screening outcomes, and no input-data requirements are specified for the instructions for use.

risks.description: Ingestion of candidate-submitted resumes, cover letters and form responses has no input validation, sanitisation or manipulation-resistance (e.g. malformed files, hidden text, prompt or adversarial injection) to protect the scoring pipeline.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.
risks.engineering_action: Add ingestion controls: file type and size checks, malware scanning, text normalisation, detection of hidden or adversarial content, and rejection or quarantine of malformed submissions. Log the outcomes.

risks.description: No handling is specified for errors or inconsistencies in ingested inputs (unparseable, incomplete or differently formatted resumes and forms), so candidates could be scored on incorrect or partial data without detection.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies that may occur within the system or the environment in which the system operates
risks.engineering_action: Define parse-failure and incompleteness handling: flag low-confidence extractions, route them to recruiter review, and never score silently on partial data.

requirement_text: The system shall provide candidates with a channel to request review of a decision that was influenced by automated ranking.

risks.engineering_action: Extend FR-10 so a review request returns a candidate-facing explanation of how the automated ranking was used and the main factors in the decision, derived from FR-4 explanations and FR-7/FR-8 records, with a defined response time.

requirement_text: The system shall generate a suitability score for each candidate based on job requirements, experience, education, and skills extracted from the application.

assessment.summary: FR-2 generates the suitability score for candidates (Annex III 4(a)) but does not define accuracy metrics, validity of the score against job-relevant criteria, or what is declared to deployers. Without these, accuracy cannot be declared or tested, and the score may rely on proxies for protected characteristics.

risks.description: No accuracy level, metrics or acceptance thresholds are specified for the suitability score, so accuracy cannot be tested or declared in the instructions for use.
risks.quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
risks.engineering_action: Define accuracy/validity metrics and minimum thresholds for the score (e.g. rank correlation with validated job-performance criteria, error rates) and include them in the instructions for use.

requirement_text: The system shall rank candidates for recruiter review using the generated suitability score.

assessment.summary: FR-3 ranks candidates from the suitability score, and the SRS already covers human override (FR-6), notification (FR-5), explanations (FR-4) and logging (FR-7). What remains is the lack of any automation-bias safeguard in the ranking presentation, and the lack of declared accuracy metrics for the ranking.

risks.description: The ranking is presented without any mechanism to make recruiters aware of automation bias (e.g. over-reliance on top-ranked candidates, or implicit auto-rejection of low-ranked ones). FR-5 notifies recruiters of automated generation, but nothing addresses over-reliance or the limits of the ranking.
risks.quote: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
risks.engineering_action: Specify in FR-3 that the ranking UI shows score uncertainty or confidence and an automation-bias warning, does not hide or auto-reject lower-ranked candidates, and provides recruiter guidance on the ranking's limitations.

requirement_text: The system shall explain the main factors that influenced each candidate suitability score in language understandable to a recruiter.

assessment.summary: FR-4 provides per-score factor explanations for recruiters, which supports interpretation of outputs. It does not define explanation fidelity or limits, and nothing makes the explanation available to affected candidates under Art. 86.

risks.description: FR-4 gives explanations only to recruiters (access limited to authorised staff by NFR-4) and covers only the score factors. requirement_text: The system shall allow a human recruiter to review, override, or reject any automated ranking before a candidate is removed from consideration.

assessment.summary: FR-6 provides a review/override/reject control, which substantively implements Art. 14(4)(d). Remaining gaps are that it does not address automation-bias awareness or oversight-person competence and authority, and does not stop the recruiter's override from being nominal or hard to perform in practice.

risks.description: No measures make recruiters aware of automation bias or over-reliance on rankings (e.g. warnings, friction, or requiring review before the ranking is acted on). FR-4 explains factors and FR-5 notifies of automated origin, but neither addresses over-reliance.
risks.quote: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
risks.engineering_action: Add UI measures against automation bias: an in-context over-reliance warning, display of score uncertainty and limitations, and monitoring of recruiter override and acceptance rates. Require a recorded rationale when the top-ranked outcome is accepted without review.

requirement_text: The system shall prevent the use of facial recognition, biometric identification, or emotion recognition during candidate screening.

assessment.summary: FR-9 is a protective control that blocks facial recognition, biometric identification and emotion recognition in screening, which supports Article 5(1)(f) compliance. The remaining gap is that it states no enforcement mechanism or verification, and it does not cover other inference routes such as emotion inference from text or voice.

risks.description: FR-9 says the system 'shall prevent' these techniques but names no technical enforcement (e.g. disabled modules, input-modality restrictions, release tests). It also does not cover emotion inference from non-facial inputs (voice, video interviews) or from other biometric data, so emotion inference in a recruitment workplace context could still occur.
risks.quote: the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions
risks.engineering_action: Reword FR-9 to prohibit inferring emotions or intentions from any biometric data (face, voice, video, behavioural signals). Enforce it by design: restrict ingestion to text documents, block biometric modalities at the input layer, and add a release test that verifies no such features are used.

assessment.summary: NFR-1 covers basic data quality checks (missing values, duplicates, label inconsistency), but it does not address bias examination, representativeness, data provenance, or documented governance. risks.quote: Testing shall be carried out against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.

requirement_text: The system shall ingest candidate resumes, cover letters, and application form responses submitted through the recruitment portal.

assessment.summary: FR-1 ingests free-text candidate documents for a high-risk recruitment system (Annex III 4(a)) without input integrity or quality controls, or data minimisation limits. Untrusted uploads and unfiltered sensitive content could degrade scoring accuracy and bypass the protected-attribute exclusion in NFR-3.

risks.description: Ingestion has no requirement for validating or sanitising uploaded files and form data (malicious files, malformed or manipulated content, prompt-injection-like text), so untrusted inputs can corrupt or manipulate downstream scoring.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.
risks.engineering_action: Add input controls to FR-1: file type and size allow-listing, malware scanning, parsing validation, and detection of hidden or adversarial text before data reaches the scoring model.

risks.description: FR-1 does not specify input data governance for operational data: no checks on relevance, representativeness or completeness of ingested applications, and no handling of parse failures or missing fields that could bias scores.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to have a negative impact on the health and safety of persons, have an adverse effect on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Define ingestion quality rules in FR-1: extraction-confidence thresholds, flagging of incomplete or unparseable applications for human handling, and format-neutral parsing so that format or language does not disadvantage candidates.

addressed_by.covers: data quality checks (missing values, duplicates, inconsistent labels), but only for training and evaluation datasets
alerts when data quality checks fall outside thresholds

risks.description: Cover letters and free-text responses may contain protected or special-category information (health, religion, political opinion) that FR-1 ingests without minimisation or filtering, so NFR-3's exclusion is not guaranteed at ingestion.
risks.quote: the providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons
risks.engineering_action: Add a pre-processing step in FR-1 that detects and redacts or segregates protected-attribute content and proxies before scoring, and document the lawful basis for any retention.

addressed_by.covers: prohibits protected attributes as ranking inputs

risks.description: FR-1 does not state that candidates are told they are subject to a high-risk AI system when submitting applications through the portal.
risks.quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
risks.engineering_action: Display a notice at the point of submission in the portal that AI-assisted screening is used, its purpose, and the review channel (FR-10).

addressed_by.covers: candidate channel to request review of AI-influenced decisions

recommendations: Add input validation, malware scanning and adversarial-content detection to FR-1.
Define ingestion data quality rules and human handling of parse failures in FR-1.
Add minimisation and redaction of protected-attribute content at ingestion.
Add a candidate-facing AI-use notice at application submission.

requirement_text: The system shall provide candidates with a channel to request review of a decision that was influenced by automated ranking.

assessment.summary: FR-10 gives candidates a review-request channel, but it does not tell candidates that automated ranking is used, does not ensure a meaningful explanation of the decision's role, and does not define how the review is handled. Candidates may not know they can request review, and the right to an explanation under Art. 86 is only partly supported.

risks.description: The requirement does not ensure that candidates are told a high-risk AI system is used in their assessment, so they may not know a review channel exists or when to use it. FR-5 notifies only recruiters.
risks.quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
risks.engineering_action: Add a candidate-facing notice at application and in decision communications that automated ranking is used, with a link to the review channel.

risks.description: The requirement offers a review channel but does not provide a clear and meaningful explanation of the role of the AI system in the decision, which affected persons are entitled to request. FR-4 explains scores only to recruiters.
risks.quote: Any affected person subject to a decision which is taken by the deployer on the basis of the output from a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III ... shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken.
risks.engineering_action: Let candidates request and receive a plain-language explanation of the ranking's role and main factors, drawn from the FR-4 output and the FR-7 logs.

addressed_by.covers: explanation of the main factors behind the score, for recruiters (basis for the candidate explanation)

risks.description: The requirement does not specify that the review is done by a competent human who can override the outcome, nor does it set review procedures such as timelines, status tracking, outcome communication and logging of review requests.
risks.quote: to decide, in any particular situation, not to use the high-risk AI system or to otherwise disregard, override or reverse the output of the high-risk AI system
risks.engineering_action: Route each review request to a trained recruiter independent of the original decision, with authority to reverse the outcome, response deadlines, and logging of requests and outcomes in the FR-7/FR-8 audit trail.

addressed_by.covers: recruiter can review, override or reject an automated ranking (14(4)(d))
logging of overrides and final decisions

recommendations: Notify candidates that automated ranking is used and link to the review channel.
Provide candidates with a plain-language explanation of the AI system's role and the main decision factors on request.
Define the review workflow: independent human reviewer, authority to override, deadlines, outcome communication, and logging of review requests.

requirement_text: The system shall generate a suitability score for each candidate based on job requirements, experience, education, and skills extracted from the application.

assessment.summary: FR-2 generates a suitability score for recruitment, which is a high-risk use (Annex III point 4). The requirement does not declare accuracy metrics for the score and has no risk management process or documented intended-purpose limits. Other SRS requirements cover explanation, logging, oversight and bias evaluation in part.

risks.description: No accuracy level or metrics are declared for the suitability score, and there is no acceptance threshold. NFR-5 alerts on thresholds that the SRS never defines.
risks.quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
risks.engineering_action: Define accuracy and validity metrics for the score, including a ranking-quality metric and per-group metrics. Set acceptance thresholds and record them in the instructions for use.

addressed_by.covers: alerts when accuracy falls outside configured thresholds (15(1) consistent performance), without defining the metrics or thresholds

risks.description: No risk management process covers the scoring function. It does not identify risks of discriminatory scoring from extracted features such as education or experience gaps, which can act as proxies for protected characteristics.
risks.quote: The risk management system shall be understood as a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system
risks.engineering_action: Set up a lifecycle risk management process for the scoring model. Cover proxy-discrimination risk from extracted features, misuse, and residual-risk acceptance, with documented mitigations.

addressed_by.covers: excludes protected attributes as ranking inputs, a partial mitigation measure under 9(5)
evaluates model performance across demographic groups, which supports the testing under 9(6)-(8)

risks.description: The requirement does not specify how skills, experience and education are extracted or what bias examination applies to them. Proxy features and extraction errors on varied resume formats are not addressed, and NFR-2 evaluates only where data is available and sets no mitigation criteria.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Specify the allowed feature set and test the extracted features for proxy bias. Define bias acceptance criteria and mitigation steps, and validate extraction accuracy across resume formats and languages.

addressed_by.covers: measures performance across demographic groups where data is available
validates training and evaluation datasets for missing values, duplicates and label inconsistencies (10(2)(g))

risks.description: The requirement does not state the intended purpose and limits of the score, such as decision support only and not a sole basis for rejection. Deployers are therefore not told how to interpret the score or what its limitations are.
risks.quote: the characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance of the high-risk AI system
risks.engineering_action: Document the intended purpose, score semantics, known limitations and appropriate use in the instructions for use. Show a score disclaimer in the recruiter UI.

addressed_by.covers: explains the main factors behind each score to recruiters (13(1) interpretability of output)
notifies recruiters that the ranking is automated

recommendations: Define accuracy and ranking-quality metrics and acceptance thresholds for the score, and declare them in the instructions for use.
Establish a lifecycle risk management process for the scoring model, covering proxy discrimination and residual risk.
Specify the allowed features, test them for proxy bias, and set bias acceptance and mitigation criteria.
Document the score's intended purpose and limitations in the instructions for use and in the recruiter UI.

requirement_text: The system shall rank candidates for recruiter review using the generated suitability score.

assessment.summary: FR-3 ranks candidates in a high-risk recruitment system (Annex III point 4). Oversight, logging, explanation and bias controls exist elsewhere in the SRS. The remaining gaps are that the ranking's accuracy and performance are not declared, and that candidates are not told they are subject to the system.

risks.description: The ranking has no declared accuracy or robustness metrics or acceptance thresholds. NFR-2 and NFR-5 measure performance and alert on thresholds, but nothing defines the ranking quality levels the system must achieve or the metrics to be declared in the instructions for use.
risks.quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
risks.engineering_action: Define ranking accuracy metrics (e.g. rank correlation against validated outcomes) and minimum acceptance levels per job category, and include them in the instructions for use.

addressed_by.covers: alerts when accuracy or bias metrics fall outside configured thresholds (15(1) consistent performance)
measurement of performance across demographic groups

risks.description: Candidates are not informed that their application is ranked by a high-risk AI system. FR-5 notifies only recruiters, and FR-10 offers review only after a decision.
risks.quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Show candidates a notice in the portal at application time that AI-assisted ranking is used, with its purpose and how to request review.

addressed_by.covers: a review channel for candidates after an automated-ranking decision (partial support for affected-person rights)

risks.description: The requirement does not state that the ranking is advisory only. Recruiters may over-rely on it (automation bias), and FR-6 only covers review before a candidate is removed.
risks.quote: remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
risks.engineering_action: Present the ranking as decision support, show score uncertainty and the FR-4 factors beside it, and add recruiter guidance on automation bias.

addressed_by.covers: review, override or rejection of the ranking (14(4)(d))
interpretation of the output (14(4)(c))

recommendations: Define ranking accuracy metrics and acceptance thresholds, and declare them in the instructions for use.
Notify candidates at application time that AI-assisted ranking is used.
Label the ranking as advisory, show the explanation factors beside it, and add automation-bias guidance for recruiters.

requirement_text: The system shall explain the main factors that influenced each candidate suitability score in language understandable to a recruiter.

assessment.summary: FR-4 gives recruiters per-score explanations, which supports transparency for deployers of a high-risk recruitment system (Annex III 4(a)). It does not specify explanation fidelity or limitations, and it does not cover the affected candidate's right to an explanation. Recruiters could over-rely on explanations that are inaccurate or incomplete.

risks.description: The requirement does not require that explanations faithfully reflect the model's actual decision logic, or that their accuracy and limitations be documented and tested. Recruiters could be misled by plausible but unfaithful explanations.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system's output and use it appropriately.
risks.engineering_action: Define explanation fidelity criteria (e.g. feature attribution consistency tests), validate them before release, and state the explanation method's limitations in the instructions for use.

risks.description: Explanations are limited to recruiters and the requirement does not address the affected candidate's right to a clear and meaningful explanation of the AI system's role in a decision. FR-10 only offers a review channel and FR-5 only notifies recruiters.
risks.quote: Any affected person subject to a decision which is taken by the deployer on the basis of the output from a high-risk AI system ... shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken.
risks.engineering_action: Add a capability to produce a candidate-facing explanation of the main elements of the decision, available on request and linked to the FR-10 review channel.

addressed_by.covers: channel for candidates to request review of decisions influenced by automated ranking

risks.description: The requirement does not tie the explanation content to the documented performance, limitations, and known risks that deployers must be given for interpreting outputs, such as the conditions under which scores are less reliable.
risks.quote: the characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance of the high-risk AI system
risks.engineering_action: Include in the explanation output, or in the instructions for use, the confidence or reliability indicators and known limitations of the score, and document them in the technical documentation.

recommendations: Specify and test explanation fidelity, and document the explanation method's limitations in the instructions for use.
Add a candidate-facing explanation capability that supports the right to explanation under Art. 86, linked to FR-10.
Surface score reliability indicators and known limitations alongside explanations.

requirement_text: The system shall notify recruiters when a candidate ranking was generated by an automated decision-support model.

assessment.summary: FR-5 tells recruiters that a ranking was machine-generated, which partly meets deployer transparency. It does not cover the system's capabilities, limitations, accuracy levels or the automation-bias warning, and it does not cover notifying candidates that a high-risk AI system is used. Candidates are not told that AI is used in decisions about them.

risks.description: FR-5 flags only that a ranking is automated. It does not require instructions for use giving recruiters the system's intended purpose, accuracy metrics, known limitations and human-oversight guidance, so recruiters cannot interpret outputs properly.
risks.quote: The instructions for use shall contain at least the following information:
risks.engineering_action: Extend FR-5 so the notification links to instructions for use covering intended purpose, accuracy levels, limitations, and oversight measures. Show this guidance in the recruiter UI.

addressed_by.covers: explains the main factors behind each score, supporting interpretability of output (13(1))

risks.description: The notification goes only to recruiters. Nothing in the SRS informs candidates, who are natural persons subject to a high-risk employment AI system, that they are subject to its use. FR-10 offers only a review channel and does not inform candidates in advance.
risks.quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Add a requirement to notify candidates, at application time and before any automated ranking is used, that an AI system assists screening. Include its purpose and how to request review.

risks.description: The notification does not warn recruiters about automation bias or require them to acknowledge it. This weakens their ability to interpret and challenge rankings.
risks.quote: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
risks.engineering_action: Include a short automation-bias caution in the notification and record that the recruiter saw it.

addressed_by.covers: lets recruiters review, override, or reject rankings (14(4)(d))

recommendations: Link the FR-5 notification to full instructions for use covering purpose, accuracy, limitations, and oversight.
Add a requirement to notify candidates that a high-risk AI system is used in screening, before use.
Add an automation-bias caution to the recruiter notification and log its display.

requirement_text: The system shall allow a human recruiter to review, override, or reject any automated ranking before a candidate is removed from consideration.

assessment.summary: FR-6 gives recruiters review, override and reject capability before a candidate is removed, which is a substantive human oversight control. Remaining gaps are about enabling effective oversight: automation bias safeguards and competence/authority of reviewers, and ensuring the override gate cannot be bypassed.

risks.description: The requirement does not guard against automation bias or require reviewers to have the competence, training and authority to override, so review could become a rubber-stamp of the ranking.
risks.quote: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
risks.engineering_action: Add UI and process safeguards against automation bias (e.g., display score confidence/limitations, require recruiter to view the explanation before confirming rejection, sample-audit approvals) and define reviewer training and authority.

addressed_by.covers: explanation of main score factors so the reviewer can interpret the output (14(4)(c))
notifies recruiters that the ranking is automated, supporting awareness of automated output (14(4)(b))

risks.description: The requirement says review occurs 'before a candidate is removed' but does not state that the system cannot auto-reject or auto-remove candidates without a recorded human action, nor does it cover a stop/interrupt capability.
risks.quote: to intervene in the operation of the high-risk AI system or interrupt the system through a 'stop' button or a similar procedure
risks.engineering_action: Enforce a workflow gate so no candidate status changes to removed without a recorded recruiter decision, and add a mechanism to pause automated ranking/screening.

addressed_by.covers: logs recruiter overrides and final screening decisions, so human actions are recorded

recommendations: Add automation-bias safeguards, reviewer competence and authority definitions to FR-6.
Enforce a hard human-decision gate before any removal and provide a mechanism to pause automated screening.

requirement_text: The system shall log every model-generated score, ranking, explanation, recruiter override, and final screening decision.

assessment.summary: FR-7 logs scores, rankings, explanations, overrides and decisions, and FR-8 adds input/model-version traceability. Remaining gaps are the missing event timestamps/user identity, no specified log retention period, and no log integrity protection.

risks.description: Logging does not specify timestamps, operator identity, model version or input reference per event, nor events relevant to identifying risk situations or substantial modifications, so traceability depends on FR-8 only for screening decisions.
risks.quote: In order to ensure a level of traceability of the functioning of a high-risk AI system that is appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, the logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk
risks.engineering_action: Define a log schema for each FR-7 event type: UTC timestamp, actor/user ID, candidate/job reference, model version, score/rank values, and override reason. Add events for risk situations such as drift alerts and rollback.

addressed_by.covers: traceability of input data, model version and human actions for each screening decision
alerts when accuracy, bias or data quality go out of threshold, which can be logged as risk events

risks.description: No log retention period is set and no tamper protection or access restriction applies to the logs themselves; deployers must keep logs for at least six months.
risks.quote: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs referred to in Article 12(1), automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems, to the extent such logs are under their control
risks.engineering_action: Specify a retention period of at least six months, configurable per legal requirements. Make logs append-only or tamper-evident, with role-based access, and reconcile retention with GDPR minimisation.

addressed_by.covers: access control on candidate data and explanations, not clearly on logs

recommendations: Specify a per-event log schema covering timestamp, actor, model version, inputs and risk events.
Define log retention of at least six months, tamper-evident storage and restricted access to logs.

requirement_text: The system shall retain audit records for each screening decision so that reviewers can trace the input data, model version, and human actions involved.

assessment.summary: FR-8 gives traceability of input, model version and human actions per screening decision, and FR-7 logs scores, overrides and decisions. What remains are retention period, log integrity and the event types Article 12 targets (risk situations, post-market monitoring), which are unspecified.

risks.description: No minimum retention period is stated for audit records; 'retain' is open-ended, so the six-month minimum for deployer-held logs (and any longer period required by law) is not guaranteed.
risks.quote: A provider of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs referred to in Article 12(1), automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems, to the extent such logs are under their control.
risks.engineering_action: Specify a configurable retention period of at least six months (longer where sector or data protection law requires), with controlled deletion consistent with GDPR.

risks.description: The requirement does not say that records are generated automatically or protected against tampering, and does not cover events that identify risk situations or substantial modifications, or events supporting post-market monitoring and deployer monitoring.
risks.quote: In order to ensure a level of traceability of the functioning of a high-risk AI system that is appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, the logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for
risks.engineering_action: Define the logged event set to include risk or anomalous outputs, model version changes and monitoring-relevant events. Make logging automatic, append-only and tamper-evident, with access restricted to authorised reviewers.

addressed_by.covers: automatic logging of scores, rankings, explanations, overrides and final decisions (Art. 12(1))
threshold alerts on accuracy, bias and data quality that feed monitoring of risk situations (Art. 12(2)(a),(c))

recommendations: Add a minimum retention period and a deletion policy to FR-8.
Specify automatic, tamper-evident logging of risk-relevant and model-change events, with restricted access.

requirement_text: The system shall prevent the use of facial recognition, biometric identification, or emotion recognition during candidate screening.

assessment.summary: FR-9 is a protective control that blocks prohibited and high-risk biometric and emotion-recognition uses in screening. It has no enforcement mechanism or verification evidence, so the prohibition on emotion inference in recruitment could be breached silently.

risks.description: FR-9 does not say how the prevention is enforced (for example blocking of video, audio, or image inputs and of inferred emotion features) or how it is verified. Emotion inference in recruitment is a prohibited practice, so an unenforced control could allow a breach.
risks.quote: the placing on the market, the putting into service for this specific purpose, or the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions
risks.engineering_action: Specify technical enforcement: restrict ingestion to text documents, reject or strip image, audio, and video inputs, and exclude inferred emotion features from the model. Add automated tests and a release gate that verify this.

risks.description: The requirement does not cover indirect biometric or emotion inference from text, or from metadata such as photos embedded in resumes. Its scope of 'during candidate screening' also leaves other recruitment stages, such as interviews, undefined.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against errors, faults or inconsistencies that may occur within the system or the environment in which the system operates
risks.engineering_action: Define scope as all recruitment stages. Add input sanitisation that removes embedded photos and biometric attachments from FR-1 ingestion, and document the prohibited-feature list in the technical documentation.

addressed_by.covers: exclusion of protected attributes as ranking inputs (partial overlap on prohibited inputs)

recommendations: Implement and test technical blocks on biometric and emotion-recognition inputs and features, with a release gate.
Extend the scope to all recruitment stages, sanitise embedded biometric data at ingestion, and record the control in the technical documentation.

requirement_text: The system must validate training and evaluation datasets for missing values, duplicate records, and inconsistent labels before model training.

assessment.summary: NFR-1 provides basic data-quality validation (missing values, duplicates, label inconsistency) for a high-risk recruitment scoring model, but does not cover the other Article 10 data governance elements: relevance and representativeness, bias examination of datasets, and documented data governance practices. No other requirement covers dataset-level bias examination or data-governance documentation, so the gap remains.

risks.description: Dataset validation covers only missing values, duplicates and label inconsistency; it omits examination of training data for biases likely to lead to discrimination in hiring, and any mitigation measures.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Extend NFR-1 with a pre-training bias examination of datasets (label and selection bias, proxy features for protected attributes) and define detection and mitigation steps with acceptance criteria.

addressed_by.covers: measures model performance across demographic groups (output-level bias check, not dataset-level examination)

risks.description: No criterion that datasets are relevant, sufficiently representative, and, to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete for the intended candidate population; the requirement has no pass/fail thresholds and says nothing about what happens when validation fails.
risks.quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose.
risks.engineering_action: Add representativeness checks against the target applicant population (roles, geography, demographics where lawful), define quantitative thresholds for completeness and error rates, and block training when they are not met.

risks.description: Validation is not tied to documented data governance practices (data origin, collection process, preparation operations, assumptions, gap identification), so there is no evidence trail for conformity assessment.
risks.quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be subject to data governance and management practices appropriate for the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Require NFR-1 to emit a versioned dataset validation report (provenance, preparation steps, assumptions, identified gaps and remediation) that is retained with the model version for technical documentation.

addressed_by.covers: traceability of input data and model version for screening decisions (not training-data provenance)

recommendations: Add dataset-level bias examination and mitigation with acceptance criteria to NFR-1.
Define representativeness and quality thresholds and block training on failure.
Generate and retain a versioned dataset validation and provenance report as part of technical documentation.

requirement_text: The system must measure model performance separately across demographic groups where lawful demographic evaluation data is available.

assessment.summary: NFR-2 measures per-group performance, which is a bias-evaluation control, but it sets no metrics, acceptance thresholds or mitigation, and the 'where lawful data is available' condition could leave bias unevaluated. Its relationship to the Article 10(5) legal basis for processing special-category data is also left unstated.

risks.description: Group-level measurement has no defined fairness metrics, acceptance criteria or required mitigation action when disparities are found, and the 'where available' condition may let evaluation be skipped entirely.
risks.quote: appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases
risks.engineering_action: Define fairness metrics and acceptance thresholds, and require documented mitigation (e.g. re-weighting, retraining, or blocking release) when thresholds are breached. Specify a fallback, such as proxy or synthetic evaluation, when demographic data is unavailable.

addressed_by.covers: alerts when bias metrics fall outside configured thresholds (detection of bias, 10(2)(g))
rollback of a model that fails fairness checks

risks.description: The requirement does not state that demographic evaluation data containing special-category data is processed only under the strict necessity and safeguard conditions for bias detection.
risks.quote: the providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons
risks.engineering_action: Specify that demographic data is used only for bias detection and correction, with access restrictions, no onward transfer, deletion once the purpose is fulfilled, and documentation of why the processing is strictly necessary.

addressed_by.covers: access controls restricting who can view candidate data

risks.description: Per-group performance is not tied to declared accuracy metrics or to the instructions for use, so deployers will not know the system's performance for specific groups.
risks.quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
risks.engineering_action: Record the per-group metrics and results in the technical documentation and instructions for use, and re-run the evaluation for each model version.

recommendations: Define fairness metrics, thresholds and mandatory mitigation or release-blocking actions, and a fallback when demographic data is unavailable.
Add Article 10(5) safeguards for any special-category data used in demographic evaluation, with purpose limitation and deletion.
Document per-group performance results in the technical documentation and instructions for use, per model version.

requirement_text: The system must not use protected attributes such as race, religion, disability, or political opinion as ranking inputs.

assessment.summary: NFR-3 excludes protected attributes as direct ranking inputs, which is a valid control. It does not address proxy variables (e.g. names, postcodes, employment gaps) that can reproduce the same bias, and it does not define how bias is examined or mitigated, so indirect discrimination in recruitment ranking could go undetected.

risks.description: Excluding only direct protected attributes leaves proxy features and correlated variables unaddressed, and NFR-3 requires no bias examination or mitigation for them. NFR-2 measures performance by group but sets no proxy detection or mitigation step.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Extend NFR-3 to require proxy-feature analysis (correlation and feature-attribution tests against protected attributes) and documented mitigation, with acceptance thresholds, before each model release.

addressed_by.covers: measures model performance separately across demographic groups, which supports bias examination (10(2)(f))
alerts when bias metrics fall outside configured thresholds (detection of bias, 10(2)(f))

risks.description: The ban on protected attributes is not tied to testing against declared fairness metrics, so no evidence shows the exclusion works in practice, and the metrics may not be declared in the documentation.
risks.quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
risks.engineering_action: Add a verification criterion to NFR-3 that tests, on a per-release basis, that ranking outputs do not depend on protected attributes or their proxies, and document the fairness metrics and results in the technical documentation and instructions for use.

addressed_by.covers: alerts when accuracy and bias metrics leave configured thresholds

recommendations: Extend NFR-3 to require proxy-feature analysis and documented mitigation, with acceptance thresholds, before each model release.
Add a per-release verification test that ranking outputs do not depend on protected attributes or their proxies, and document the fairness metrics and results in the technical documentation.

requirement_text: The system must maintain access controls so that only authorised recruitment staff can view candidate data and model explanations.

assessment.summary: NFR-4 restricts viewing of candidate data and explanations to authorised recruitment staff, which is a substantive confidentiality control. The remaining gaps are that it does not cover the logs and audit records (FR-7, FR-8) or the model and training artefacts, and that it says nothing about integrity controls or access logging.

risks.description: Access control covers only candidate data and model explanations; it does not extend to the logs, audit records, model versions, or training/evaluation datasets, nor does it require integrity protection against unauthorised modification or tampering.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.
risks.engineering_action: Extend the access control scope to audit logs, model registry, and training/evaluation datasets. Enforce role-based least privilege with write/modify separation, and add integrity protection (e.g. tamper-evident logs, signed model artefacts).

risks.description: The requirement does not state that access attempts (view, export, denied access) are logged or that 'authorised' roles are defined, so unauthorised access to personal candidate data and explanations cannot be reliably detected or traced.
risks.quote: In order to ensure a level of traceability of the functioning of a high-risk AI system that is appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk
risks.engineering_action: Define authorised roles explicitly, and log access events (user, time, record, action, denial) to the audit trail, with periodic access review.

addressed_by.covers: logging of scores, rankings, explanations, overrides and final decisions (not access events)

recommendations: Extend access control and add integrity protections to logs, model artefacts, and datasets, not only candidate data and explanations.
Define authorised roles and log all access events, including denied attempts, in the audit trail.

requirement_text: The system must produce monitoring alerts when model accuracy, bias metrics, or data quality checks fall outside configured thresholds.

assessment.summary: NFR-5 provides threshold-based alerts but does not say who receives or acts on them, how thresholds are set and justified, or how alerts feed incident handling and post-market monitoring. Without these, drift or bias in a high-risk recruitment (Annex III 4) system could go unaddressed and unreported.

risks.description: Alerts are not tied to a documented post-market monitoring plan: no systematic collection and analysis of performance data over the system lifetime, and no defined recipients or response actions.
risks.quote: The post-market monitoring system shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data
risks.engineering_action: Define alert owners, escalation SLAs and response playbooks. Feed alert and metric data into a documented post-market monitoring plan with periodic review.

addressed_by.covers: logging of scores, rankings and decisions that can serve as post-market data

risks.description: Alert thresholds for accuracy and bias are only 'configured', with no requirement to derive them from declared accuracy metrics or to document and approve them. They also do not cover robustness or feedback-loop drift.
risks.quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
risks.engineering_action: Set thresholds from the declared accuracy and fairness metrics, version and approve changes to them, and add drift and robustness indicators. Document thresholds in the instructions for use.

addressed_by.covers: per-group performance measurement that supplies the bias metrics (Art. 15(3))

risks.description: A threshold breach does not trigger risk management actions, such as a rollback decision or a serious-incident assessment. NFR-6 covers rollback but is not linked to the alerts.
risks.quote: the evaluation of other risks possibly arising, based on the analysis of data gathered from the post-market monitoring system referred to in Article 72
risks.engineering_action: Specify that critical alerts open a risk-review ticket, can trigger the NFR-6 rollback, and are assessed against serious-incident criteria (Art. 73).

addressed_by.covers: rollback to an approved model version when checks fail (risk mitigation measure, Art. 9(5))

recommendations: Define alert recipients, escalation SLAs and a post-market monitoring plan that consumes alert data.
Derive alert thresholds from declared accuracy and fairness metrics, version them, and add drift and robustness indicators.
Link critical alerts to risk review, NFR-6 rollback and serious-incident assessment.

requirement_text: The system should support rollback to a previously approved model version if a deployed model fails safety, robustness, or fairness checks.

assessment.summary: NFR-6 provides a rollback control but does not define the trigger criteria, who approves a rollback, or how rollback events are recorded. The pass/fail thresholds and the rollback event trail are therefore unspecified for a high-risk recruitment system (Annex III 4(a)).

risks.description: Rollback is triggered by 'safety, robustness, or fairness checks' with no defined metrics, thresholds, or acceptance criteria, and it is not linked to NFR-5 alerts, so the declared accuracy and robustness levels cannot be enforced.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, and that they perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle.
risks.engineering_action: Define quantitative pass/fail criteria for the safety, robustness and fairness checks (reusing the NFR-2 and NFR-5 thresholds). State that a threshold breach triggers a rollback review, and set the maximum time to complete it.

addressed_by.covers: monitoring alerts when accuracy, bias metrics or data quality fall outside configured thresholds (detection side of 15(1))

risks.description: The requirement does not say that rollback events (trigger, approver, source and target model version, time) are logged or that the approved-version registry is kept. Traceability of which model version produced a decision may break after a rollback.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.
risks.engineering_action: Log every rollback and version change as an event, with trigger reason, approver, and from/to model versions. Keep these records alongside the FR-8 audit records.

addressed_by.covers: traceability of the model version used for each screening decision
logging of model-generated scores and rankings

risks.description: The requirement does not say that a rollback or a model version change is documented, or that a substantial modification is assessed. Reverting to or redeploying a model may alter the system's performance and its documented behaviour.
risks.quote: The technical documentation of a high-risk AI system shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market or put into service and shall be kept up-to-date.
risks.engineering_action: Require that the model version register and technical documentation are updated after each rollback. Define 'previously approved' as a version with recorded validation evidence, and include the rollback procedure in the change-management process.

recommendations: Define quantitative rollback trigger criteria tied to the NFR-2 and NFR-5 thresholds, and set a response time.
Log rollback events with trigger, approver and from/to model versions, and keep them linked to the FR-8 audit records.
Keep a register of approved model versions with validation evidence, and update the technical documentation after each rollback.

requirement_text: The system shall ingest candidate resumes, cover letters, and application form responses submitted through the recruitment portal.

assessment.summary: FR-1 ingests free-text candidate resumes, cover letters and form responses for a recruitment (Annex III point 4(a)) high-risk system, but states no input data quality or integrity controls. Untrusted, unstructured uploads could be manipulated or carry errors and bias into scoring, which affects robustness and fairness.

risks.description: Ingested candidate documents and form responses are untrusted inputs. FR-1 specifies no validation, sanitisation or malicious-content handling, so tampered or adversarial files (e.g. hidden text, prompt or keyword injection) could alter scores or outputs.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.
risks.engineering_action: Add input controls at ingestion: file type/size limits, malware scanning, stripping hidden or non-visible text, detection of adversarial or injected content, and a quarantine path for flagged submissions.

addressed_by.covers: alerts when accuracy or data quality fall outside thresholds, detecting degraded performance (15(1) consistency), not input manipulation

risks.description: FR-1 does not define how ingested production inputs are checked for completeness, errors or representativeness (e.g. parsing failures, non-standard formats, non-native language), which can systematically disadvantage some candidates. NFR-1 covers only training and evaluation datasets, not live input data.
risks.quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose.
risks.engineering_action: Specify input quality checks at ingestion: parsing-failure detection with human fallback, supported formats and languages, completeness checks, and monitoring of extraction error rates across candidate groups.

addressed_by.covers: validation of training and evaluation datasets for missing values, duplicates and inconsistent labels
performance measured across demographic groups

recommendations: Add ingestion-time input integrity and adversarial-content controls to FR-1 (file validation, malware scanning, hidden-text stripping, quarantine).
Define input data quality checks and parsing-failure handling in FR-1, and monitor extraction error rates across candidate groups.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall provide candidates with a channel to request review of a decision that was influenced by automated ranking.

assessment.summary: FR-10 provides a review channel for candidates but does not tell candidates they are subject to the high-risk system, and it leaves the review process undefined (explanation of the AI's role, reviewer, timelines). Without these, candidates cannot effectively use the channel and the deployer's Article 26(11) and 86 obligations are not met.

risks.description: No requirement informs candidates that they are subject to an AI-assisted ranking system; FR-5 notifies only recruiters, so candidates may not know a review channel is relevant to them.
risks.quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
risks.engineering_action: Amend FR-10 (or add a requirement) so candidates are told at application time and again in decision communications that automated ranking is used, with a link to the review channel.

risks.description: The review channel does not require that candidates receive a clear and meaningful explanation of the AI system's role in the decision and the main elements of the decision; FR-4 explains factors only to recruiters.
risks.quote: shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken.
risks.engineering_action: Specify that a review request returns a candidate-facing explanation of the role of the ranking and the main decision elements, generated from FR-4 factors and FR-7/FR-8 records.

addressed_by.covers: explanation of main factors behind each score (recruiter-facing only)
traceability of input data, model version and human actions needed to build the explanation

risks.description: FR-10 does not require that review requests be handled by a competent human with authority to override, nor define outcome, timelines or logging of review requests.
risks.quote: to decide, in any particular situation, not to use the high-risk AI system or to otherwise disregard, override or reverse the output of the high-risk AI system;
risks.engineering_action: State that reviews are assigned to a trained recruiter independent of the original decision, who can disregard or reverse the ranking, with response deadlines and logged outcomes.

addressed_by.covers: recruiter ability to review, override or reject automated ranking before removal
logging of recruiter overrides and final decisions

recommendations: Inform candidates they are subject to AI-assisted ranking, at application and in decision notices, and link to the review channel.
Provide candidate-facing explanations of the AI system's role and the main decision elements on review requests.
Define review handling: independent competent reviewer, override authority, response timelines, and logging of review outcomes.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall generate a suitability score for each candidate based on job requirements, experience, education, and skills extracted from the application.

assessment.summary: FR-2 generates suitability scores for recruitment (Annex III 4(a), high-risk) but does not specify accuracy metrics or declared accuracy levels, input robustness/integrity controls, or bias-prone proxy handling for the extracted features. Without these, the scoring model cannot be shown to meet Article 15 and Article 10 expectations.

risks.description: No accuracy level or accuracy metrics are specified for the suitability score, so none can be declared in the instructions for use or validated against a target.
risks.quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
risks.engineering_action: Define accuracy metrics and target levels for the scoring model (e.g. rank correlation with recruiter-validated outcomes, per-group error rates), set acceptance thresholds, and include them in the instructions for use.

addressed_by.covers: monitoring of model accuracy against configured thresholds (supports 15(1) consistent performance over lifecycle, not declaration of levels)

risks.description: Scores are computed from features extracted from free-form applications, with no requirement for resilience against erroneous or manipulated inputs (e.g. keyword stuffing, adversarial or hidden text, parsing errors).
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.
risks.engineering_action: Add robustness requirements for the extraction and scoring pipeline: input sanitisation, detection of hidden or injected text and adversarial resume patterns, and adversarial testing with pass criteria.

addressed_by.covers: access control over candidate data (limits unauthorised access, not manipulation of submitted inputs)

risks.description: Extraction of education, experience and skills as scoring features can encode proxies for protected characteristics (age, gender, nationality, disability), and FR-2 specifies no bias examination or mitigation of these features; NFR-3 only excludes direct protected attributes.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Require a proxy-feature and bias examination of the scoring features (e.g. education institution, employment gaps, name or location signals), with documented mitigation and acceptance criteria for score disparities.

addressed_by.covers: measurement of model performance across demographic groups
exclusion of protected attributes as ranking inputs
dataset validation for missing values, duplicates, inconsistent labels

recommendations: Specify accuracy metrics, target levels and acceptance thresholds for the suitability score, and declare them in the instructions for use.
Add input-robustness and adversarial-manipulation requirements for the resume extraction and scoring pipeline, with test criteria.
Add proxy-feature bias examination and mitigation with acceptance criteria for scoring features, beyond direct protected-attribute exclusion.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall rank candidates for recruiter review using the generated suitability score.

assessment.summary: FR-3 ranks candidates by suitability score in an Annex III point 4(a) high-risk recruitment context. Human review (FR-6), explanation (FR-4), logging (FR-7) and bias controls (NFR-2/3/5) exist elsewhere, but FR-3 itself leaves open how ranking accuracy is declared and how ranking-specific bias and feedback loops are handled.

risks.description: No accuracy level or metrics are specified or declared for the ranking function (e.g. ranking quality, consistency across the lifecycle); NFR-5 only alerts on thresholds that FR-3 never defines.
risks.quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
risks.engineering_action: Define ranking accuracy/robustness metrics and target thresholds for FR-3, test against them before release, and declare them in the instructions for use.

addressed_by.covers: monitoring of accuracy against configured thresholds (15(1) consistent performance throughout lifecycle)
performance measured separately across demographic groups

risks.description: Ranking outputs may feed back into future model training or tuning (e.g. recruiter selections following ranked order) with no stated mitigation of biased feedback loops or ranking-position effects.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market or put into service shall be developed in such a way as to eliminate or reduce as far as possible the risk of possibly biased outputs influencing input for future operations (feedback loops)
risks.engineering_action: Specify that ranking outcomes and recruiter actions are not reused as training labels without bias review, and add feedback-loop detection and mitigation for the ranking model.

addressed_by.covers: alerts when bias metrics fall outside thresholds

risks.description: The ranking itself is not tied to a bias examination covering ranking-level discrimination (e.g. proxy variables, disparate ranking positions); NFR-3 excludes protected attributes but not proxies, and NFR-2 measures performance, not ranking outcomes.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Add acceptance criteria for FR-3 ranking outcomes (e.g. selection-rate parity across groups, proxy-feature analysis) and define mitigation measures when thresholds are breached.

addressed_by.covers: per-group performance measurement (bias examination)
exclusion of protected attributes as inputs
dataset validation for missing values, duplicates, inconsistent labels

recommendations: Define and declare ranking accuracy/robustness metrics and thresholds for FR-3 in the instructions for use.
Prevent ranking outcomes from silently becoming training data; add feedback-loop detection and mitigation.
Add ranking-level bias acceptance criteria, proxy-variable analysis, and mitigation actions.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall explain the main factors that influenced each candidate suitability score in language understandable to a recruiter.

assessment.summary: FR-4 gives recruiters plain-language explanations of score drivers, which supports transparency and oversight. The wording does not require that explanations are faithful to the model, nor that limitations are conveyed. It also does not support the right to explanation for affected candidates. Recruiters could over-rely on misleading explanations.

risks.description: FR-4 does not require that explanations be accurate and faithful to the model, or that they state limitations, confidence and known circumstances affecting reliability, so recruiters may misinterpret scores or over-rely on them (automation bias).
risks.quote: where applicable, the technical capabilities and characteristics of the high-risk AI system to provide information that is relevant to explain its output
risks.engineering_action: Specify that explanations are derived from the actual scoring model (feature attribution validated for fidelity), and include score confidence, known limitations and accuracy caveats. Document explanation capabilities in the instructions for use.

addressed_by.covers: notifies recruiters that a ranking was produced by an automated decision-support model (partial awareness of automated output)

risks.description: The requirement does not tie explanations to enabling overseers to correctly interpret outputs and stay aware of automation bias (e.g. no guidance on overriding or on disagreement indicators).
risks.quote: to correctly interpret the high-risk AI system’s output, taking into account, for example, the interpretation tools and methods available
risks.engineering_action: Add acceptance criteria that explanations support recruiter interpretation (usability testing with recruiters), include automation-bias warnings in the UI, and link explanations to the override flow.

addressed_by.covers: recruiter can review, override or reject rankings (14(4)(d))

risks.description: Explanations are scoped to recruiters only; no requirement lets the deployer give affected candidates a clear and meaningful explanation of the AI's role in a decision, and the explanation is not stored in a form that can be reproduced for such a request.
risks.quote: shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken
risks.engineering_action: Add a capability to produce a candidate-facing explanation of the AI's role and main decision elements, reusing the stored FR-4 explanation, and make it available to the deployer on request.

addressed_by.covers: channel for candidates to request review of a decision influenced by automated ranking
logs model-generated explanations, so they can be retrieved

recommendations: Require explanations to be faithful to the scoring model and to state confidence and limitations, and document this in the instructions for use.
Validate that explanations help recruiters interpret scores, add automation-bias warnings, and connect explanations to the override workflow.
Add a candidate-facing explanation output for deployers, built on the stored recruiter explanation, to support Article 86 requests.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall notify recruiters when a candidate ranking was generated by an automated decision-support model.

assessment.summary: FR-5 notifies recruiters that a ranking is automated, which supports interpretation and awareness of automation bias. It does not cover the candidates, who are never told that a high-risk Annex III recruitment system is used on them, and it does not say whether the recruiter notice includes information needed to use the output appropriately.

risks.description: Only recruiters are notified; candidates subject to the Annex III point 4(a) recruitment system are not informed that they are subject to its use, and no other requirement provides this notice.
risks.quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Add a requirement to notify candidates, before or at application submission and in the decision communication, that an automated ranking system is used in screening. Make the notice clear and accessible.

risks.description: The notification is a bare flag that a ranking was machine-generated. It does not state that recruiters must be told the system's limitations, accuracy level, or the risk of over-reliance on its output, so it does not by itself enable appropriate use or awareness of automation bias.
risks.quote: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
risks.engineering_action: Extend the recruiter notification to include a short automation-bias caution and a pointer to the score's limitations and accuracy information. Also cover this in the instructions for use and reviewer training.

addressed_by.covers: explains main factors behind each score so recruiters can interpret the output (14(4)(c))
recruiter can disregard, override or reverse the output (14(4)(d))

recommendations: Add a candidate-facing notice that the recruitment screening uses an automated ranking system (Art. 26(11)).
Expand the recruiter notification to include a limitations and automation-bias caution linked to accuracy information (Art. 14(4)(b)).

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall allow a human recruiter to review, override, or reject any automated ranking before a candidate is removed from consideration.

assessment.summary: FR-6 gives recruiters review/override/reject capability, which is a substantive human oversight control, but it does not address automation bias awareness, a stop/interrupt capability, or recruiter competence and authority. The remaining gaps are narrow, since FR-4, FR-5 and FR-7 cover interpretation, notification and logging.

risks.description: FR-6 requires no mechanism to keep recruiters aware of automation bias or over-reliance on rankings (e.g. rubber-stamping top-ranked candidates), and does not oblige a human review step in practice. 'Allow' to review does not ensure rankings are actually reviewed before exclusion.
risks.quote: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
risks.engineering_action: Require an explicit recorded recruiter confirmation before any candidate is removed, add automation-bias warnings in the UI and in the instructions for use, and monitor override and acceptance rates for signs of rubber-stamping.

addressed_by.covers: helps the recruiter correctly interpret the output by explaining the main score factors (14(4)(c))
flags to recruiters that a ranking came from an automated model (partial awareness of the system's role)

risks.description: FR-6 covers per-candidate override but gives no ability to halt or suspend the ranking model or the batch process (a 'stop' or safe-halt) when anomalies are detected.
risks.quote: to intervene in the operation of the high-risk AI system or interrupt the system through a ‘stop’ button or a similar procedure that allows the system to come to a halt in a safe state
risks.engineering_action: Add an operator-accessible control to pause or disable automated ranking and fall back to manual screening.

addressed_by.covers: rollback to an approved model version on failed checks (partial intervention capability, not a user-initiated stop)

risks.description: The requirement does not specify that the reviewing recruiters have the competence, training and authority to override, nor that the system supports their understanding of its capacities and limitations.
risks.quote: to properly understand the relevant capacities and limitations of the high-risk AI system and be able to duly monitor its operation, including in view of detecting and addressing anomalies, dysfunctions and unexpected performance
risks.engineering_action: Document in the instructions for use the reviewer competence and training required, and provide in-tool guidance on model limitations; define reviewer authority to override without penalty.

addressed_by.covers: alerts on accuracy, bias and data quality threshold breaches, supporting detection of anomalies

recommendations: Make human confirmation mandatory and recorded before exclusion, and add automation-bias safeguards and override-rate monitoring.
Add a pause or disable control for automated ranking with a manual fallback.
Specify reviewer competence, training and authority in the instructions for use and provide in-tool guidance on model limitations.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall log every model-generated score, ranking, explanation, recruiter override, and final screening decision.

assessment.summary: FR-7 covers the main logged events (scores, rankings, explanations, overrides, decisions) for a recruitment system (Annex III 4(a)). It does not state a retention period, which Art. 19/26(6) require to be at least six months. It also does not tie the logs to Art. 12(2) purposes or protect their integrity.

risks.description: No log retention period is specified; the requirement does not ensure logs are kept for at least six months or an appropriate period for the intended purpose.
risks.quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
risks.engineering_action: Add a retention requirement: logs kept at least 6 months, or longer where justified by intended purpose, with deletion rules aligned with data protection law.

addressed_by.covers: retains audit records of each screening decision so reviewers can trace input data, model version and human actions (partial retention of traceability data, no period stated)

risks.description: The logged events are not linked to Art. 12(2) purposes. Events that identify risk situations or substantial modifications, support post-market monitoring, and support deployer monitoring are not covered, e.g. model version, input data reference, threshold breaches, drift, and model changes or rollbacks.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for: (a) identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk
risks.engineering_action: Extend the logged event set to include model version, input reference, timestamps, monitoring-threshold breaches, model deployment/rollback events, and state that logs support post-market monitoring and deployer monitoring.

addressed_by.covers: traceability of input data and model version per screening decision (Art. 12(2) traceability)

risks.description: The requirement does not specify protection of log integrity, such as tamper-evidence and restricted access. Logs contain candidate personal data and recruiter actions that authorities may later request.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.
risks.engineering_action: Specify automatic, append-only or tamper-evident logging over the system lifetime, with access restricted to authorised roles, and the ability to export logs to competent authorities on request.

addressed_by.covers: access controls limiting who can view candidate data and model explanations

recommendations: Add a log retention period of at least six months, with data-protection-compliant deletion.
Extend the logged events to the Art. 12(2) purposes, including model version, monitoring threshold breaches and model changes.
Make logs tamper-evident and access-controlled, and exportable to authorities on request.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall retain audit records for each screening decision so that reviewers can trace the input data, model version, and human actions involved.

assessment.summary: FR-8 retains audit records for tracing input data, model version and human actions, and FR-7 already logs scores, rankings, explanations, overrides and decisions. Remaining gaps are the unspecified retention period and the missing tie to Article 12(2) risk and post-market monitoring events.

risks.description: No retention period is set for audit records, so they could be deleted before the Article 19 minimum of six months (and, for provider documentation, before the Article 18 period).
risks.quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
risks.engineering_action: Add a retention requirement of at least six months, longer where the intended purpose needs it, subject to data protection law. Make audit records tamper-evident and available to authorities on request.

risks.description: FR-8 defines audit records only for tracing individual screening decisions. It does not require recording events that identify risk situations, substantial modifications, or support post-market monitoring and deployer monitoring (e.g. threshold breaches, model version changes, rollbacks).
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for: (a) identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk
