risks.engineering_action: Extend FR-8 to record system-level events: model version deployments and changes, rollbacks, monitoring alert triggers, and anomalies. Define the log schema so it supports post-market monitoring and deployer monitoring.

addressed_by.covers: automatic logging of model scores, rankings, explanations, recruiter overrides and final decisions over the system's operation (12(1))

recommendations: Specify an audit-record retention period of at least six months, with integrity protection and authority access.
Extend audit records to cover model version changes, rollbacks and monitoring alert events so they support Article 12(2) traceability.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall prevent the use of facial recognition, biometric identification, or emotion recognition during candidate screening.

assessment.summary: FR-9 is a protective control that blocks facial recognition, biometric identification and emotion recognition in candidate screening, which keeps the system clear of Article 5(1)(f) and Annex III point 1. Only minor gaps remain: how the prevention is verified and documented, and how the restriction is communicated to deployers.

risks.description: FR-9 does not say how the prevention is enforced or verified (for example, which inputs such as video or images are blocked or ignored, or whether the system can infer emotion from text or audio). It also sets no acceptance test or documented evidence of the prevention, and no handling for reasonably foreseeable misuse.
risks.quote: the estimation and evaluation of the risks that may emerge when the high-risk AI system is used in accordance with its intended purpose, and under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse
risks.engineering_action: Define technical enforcement for FR-9 (reject or strip image, video and audio inputs, and exclude emotion-inference features). Add test cases against misuse and record the results in the risk management file and technical documentation.

risks.description: The exclusion of biometric and emotion-recognition functions is not stated as a limitation or intended-purpose boundary in the instructions for use provided to deployers.
risks.quote: the characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance of the high-risk AI system, including: (i) its intended purpose
risks.engineering_action: State in the instructions for use that facial recognition, biometric identification and emotion recognition are disabled and out of scope. Warn deployers that enabling them would change the system's classification and compliance obligations.

recommendations: Specify and test the technical mechanism that enforces FR-9 and keep the evidence in the risk management file.
Document the biometric and emotion-recognition exclusion in the instructions for use as a stated limitation.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system must validate training and evaluation datasets for missing values, duplicate records, and inconsistent labels before model training.

assessment.summary: NFR-1 provides a basic data-quality check (missing values, duplicates, inconsistent labels) but does not cover the other Article 10 data governance elements. Representativeness, bias examination of the datasets and gap identification are not required. For a recruitment ranking system (Annex III point 4), unaddressed dataset bias could lead to discriminatory screening.

risks.description: Dataset checks cover only missing values, duplicates and label inconsistency; there is no examination of the training/validation/testing data for biases likely to cause discrimination, and no measures to detect, prevent or mitigate them.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Extend the dataset validation step to include a documented bias examination of training, validation and testing data (e.g. label and outcome skew by group, proxy features) with defined mitigation actions and acceptance criteria before training proceeds.

addressed_by.covers: measures model performance across demographic groups, a model-level bias evaluation after training (not a dataset bias examination)
excludes protected attributes as ranking inputs, a partial bias prevention measure

risks.description: The requirement does not require checking that datasets are relevant, sufficiently representative and have appropriate statistical properties for the candidate population, nor does it require identifying data gaps or shortcomings.
risks.quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose.
risks.engineering_action: Add validation criteria for representativeness and statistical properties against the intended applicant population and job context, and a gap/shortcoming register (Art. 10(2)(h)) with remediation steps. Define pass/fail thresholds that gate model training.

risks.description: The requirement does not mandate documented data governance practices (data origin, collection, labelling and preparation operations, assumptions, suitability assessment) or recording of validation results.
risks.quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be subject to data governance and management practices appropriate for the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Require that validation results, dataset provenance, labelling and preparation steps and design assumptions are recorded and versioned as part of technical documentation.

addressed_by.covers: retains audit records tracing input data and model version for screening decisions (operational traceability, not training-dataset governance)

recommendations: Add a documented dataset bias examination and mitigation step with acceptance criteria to NFR-1.
Add representativeness, statistical-property and data-gap checks as gating criteria before training.
Record dataset provenance, preparation steps, assumptions and validation results as versioned technical documentation.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system must measure model performance separately across demographic groups where lawful demographic evaluation data is available.

assessment.summary: NFR-2 measures per-group performance only where lawful demographic data exists. It sets no acceptance thresholds, no mitigation duty, and no fallback when demographic data is absent, and it does not tie the measurement to bias examination of data sets or to declared metrics. Without these, bias in a recruitment-screening system could go undetected or unaddressed.

risks.description: Per-group performance is measured but there are no acceptance criteria or thresholds, and no defined action when disparities are found. NFR-5 alerts on bias metrics against configured thresholds, but nothing says what counts as an acceptable group disparity or what mitigation follows.
risks.quote: appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases identified according to point (f);
risks.engineering_action: Define per-group metrics, maximum tolerated disparity thresholds and a required mitigation and re-test workflow. Block model release when thresholds are exceeded.

addressed_by.covers: monitoring alerts when bias metrics fall outside configured thresholds
rollback of a model version that fails fairness checks

risks.description: The 'where lawful demographic data is available' qualifier leaves no alternative bias-examination method (e.g. proxy analysis or synthetic data) when such data is absent. Bias could then go unexamined for some groups. Any use of special-category data for bias detection must also meet the Article 10(5) safeguards, which the requirement does not mention.
risks.quote: the providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons.
risks.engineering_action: Specify the fallback bias-examination approach when demographic data is unavailable. If special-category data is used, state the Article 10(5) conditions: necessity, access controls, no onward transfer, deletion after use and records of processing.

addressed_by.covers: access controls limiting who can view candidate data

risks.description: The requirement does not say that per-group accuracy results must be tested against predefined metrics or declared in the instructions for use. Evaluation of group-specific performance is therefore not linked to the declared accuracy levels and group performance disclosure.
risks.quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
risks.engineering_action: Require that the per-group metrics and results are recorded in the technical documentation and in the instructions for use, including performance for specific groups.

recommendations: Define per-group metrics, disparity thresholds and a mandatory mitigation and re-test step before release.
Define a fallback bias-examination method when demographic data is unavailable, and document Article 10(5) safeguards if special-category data is used.
Record per-group accuracy metrics and results in the technical documentation and instructions for use.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system must not use protected attributes such as race, religion, disability, or political opinion as ranking inputs.

assessment.summary: NFR-3 excludes protected attributes as direct ranking inputs, which is a real bias control, but it does not address proxy variables, bias examination of the data, or mitigation. Resume-derived features (names, schools, gaps, location) can act as proxies and still produce discriminatory rankings in this Annex III(4)(a) recruitment system.

risks.description: Excluding only explicit protected attributes does not cover proxy features (e.g., name, address, school, employment gaps) inferred from resumes, and no examination of training data for correlated bias is specified.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Extend NFR-3 to require proxy-variable analysis (correlation/feature-attribution tests against protected attributes) and exclusion or neutralisation of identified proxies in feature extraction and training data.

addressed_by.covers: dataset validation for missing values, duplicates and inconsistent labels (data quality part of Art. 10(3))

risks.description: The requirement prevents use of protected attributes but sets no measures to detect, prevent and mitigate biases found, such as acceptance criteria or remediation when proxy effects are detected.
risks.quote: appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases identified according to point (f)
risks.engineering_action: Add a verifiable criterion that ranking outputs show no statistically significant disparate impact by protected group, with a defined mitigation workflow (re-weighting, feature removal, retraining) when thresholds are breached.

addressed_by.covers: detection of performance differences across demographic groups
alerts when bias metrics exceed configured thresholds

risks.description: Protected attributes may be needed for bias testing yet NFR-3 gives no rule on how they are held separately from ranking inputs, so the exclusion boundary between ranking and evaluation use is unclear.
risks.quote: the providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons
risks.engineering_action: Clarify that protected attributes may be used only in an access-restricted evaluation environment for bias detection, with documented necessity, pseudonymisation and deletion once bias is corrected, and never as model features.

addressed_by.covers: access control on candidate data

recommendations: Add proxy-variable detection and neutralisation to NFR-3 and the feature pipeline.
Define fairness acceptance criteria and a mitigation workflow triggered when bias thresholds are breached.
Specify that protected attributes are used only in a restricted evaluation environment with Art. 10(5) safeguards, never as ranking features.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system must maintain access controls so that only authorised recruitment staff can view candidate data and model explanations.

assessment.summary: NFR-4 restricts viewing of candidate data and explanations to authorised recruitment staff, which is a basic access control. It does not address resilience against unauthorised third-party manipulation of the system's use, outputs or performance, and it does not tie access to the competence and authority required for oversight.

risks.description: Access control covers only viewing of candidate data and explanations. It does not cover protection of the model, scoring pipeline, training data or outputs against unauthorised alteration or manipulation (data/model poisoning, adversarial inputs, tampering with scores or logs).
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.
risks.engineering_action: Extend NFR-4 or add a cybersecurity requirement covering write and modify access to models, datasets, scores and logs. Include role-based least privilege, authentication, integrity protection, and controls against data poisoning, model poisoning and adversarial inputs.

addressed_by.covers: records model scores, rankings, overrides and decisions, which supports detection of tampering after the fact

risks.description: 'Authorised recruitment staff' is not defined. Access is not linked to the competence, training and authority needed for human oversight, and it does not state which roles may view explanations and override rankings.
risks.quote: to properly understand the relevant capacities and limitations of the high-risk AI system and be able to duly monitor its operation
risks.engineering_action: Define the roles permitted to access candidate data and explanations, and make access conditional on completed training and assigned oversight authority. Ensure that persons who oversee and override rankings (FR-6) keep the access they need to explanations.

addressed_by.covers: explains the main factors behind each score to the recruiter, so oversight personnel can interpret outputs (14(4)(c))
allows the recruiter to review, override or reject automated rankings (14(4)(d))

recommendations: Extend access controls to cover integrity protection and unauthorised modification of the model, data, scores and logs, and add defences against data poisoning, model poisoning and adversarial inputs.
Define the authorised roles and tie access to training and oversight authority, so that overseers retain access to explanations.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system must produce monitoring alerts when model accuracy, bias metrics, or data quality checks fall outside configured thresholds.

assessment.summary: NFR-5 provides threshold-based alerts on accuracy, bias and data quality for a high-risk recruitment ranking system (Annex III 4(a)). It does not say how thresholds are set, who receives alerts, what response follows, or how alert data feeds post-market monitoring and risk management. Without these, the alerts may not support continuous-compliance evaluation.

risks.description: Alerts only fire on configured thresholds. The requirement does not define how thresholds are derived from declared accuracy metrics and acceptance criteria, so the monitoring may not detect drift from the declared performance.
risks.quote: they perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle
risks.engineering_action: Derive alert thresholds from pre-defined accuracy, robustness and bias metrics and acceptance criteria. Document them in the technical documentation and instructions for use, and re-baseline them when the model or data changes.

addressed_by.covers: measures model performance separately across demographic groups, giving the bias metrics that alerts can monitor

risks.description: Alerts are not tied to a post-market monitoring system or plan. There is no systematic collection and analysis of performance data over the system's lifetime to evaluate continuous compliance, and no defined recipient or response to an alert.
risks.quote: shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data which may be provided by deployers or which may be collected through other sources on the performance of high-risk AI systems throughout their lifetime
risks.engineering_action: Specify that alerts feed a documented post-market monitoring plan. Define alert owners, triage and escalation SLAs, and a link to rollback and corrective action. Retain alert history as monitoring evidence.

addressed_by.covers: rollback to a previously approved model version when checks fail, a corrective action following a monitoring finding

risks.description: Alert events and threshold breaches are not specified as logged events. They therefore may not be recorded to identify risk situations or to support post-market monitoring.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for: (a) identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk
risks.engineering_action: Log every alert (metric, threshold, value, model version, timestamp, acknowledgement and action taken) and retain these logs for at least six months.

addressed_by.covers: logs model-generated scores, rankings, explanations, overrides and final decisions

recommendations: Define alert thresholds from declared accuracy, robustness and fairness metrics and document them.
Link alerts to a post-market monitoring plan with named owners, escalation and corrective-action procedures.
Log all alert events with model version and response actions, and retain them.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system should support rollback to a previously approved model version if a deployed model fails safety, robustness, or fairness checks.

assessment.summary: NFR-6 provides rollback to an approved model version, which supports corrective action and resilience. The remaining gaps are that it is unspecified (no rollback triggers, no fail-safe behaviour, no thresholds), is only 'should', and does not tie the check results to approved criteria or to the compliance documentation.

risks.description: Rollback is triggered by undefined 'safety, robustness, or fairness checks' with no prior-defined metrics or probabilistic thresholds, and NFR-5 only alerts on thresholds rather than defining pass/fail criteria for approving or rolling back a version.
risks.quote: Testing shall be carried out against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Define in NFR-6 the metrics, thresholds and acceptance criteria (accuracy, robustness, per-group fairness) that determine whether a version is approved and when rollback is mandatory.

addressed_by.covers: alerts when accuracy, bias metrics or data quality fall outside configured thresholds (detection only, not approval criteria)

risks.description: The requirement does not specify the robustness behaviour of the rollback mechanism, such as a safe fallback while rolling back, integrity protection of the approved version registry, or prevention of unauthorised version changes.
risks.quote: The robustness of high-risk AI systems may be achieved through technical redundancy solutions, which may include backup or fail-safe plans.
risks.engineering_action: Specify a fail-safe state (e.g. pause automated ranking and route to manual review) during rollback, signed/immutable approved-version artifacts, and access control on rollback actions.

addressed_by.covers: access controls limiting who can view candidate data and explanations (not model version management)

risks.description: The requirement does not state that rollback events and version changes are logged or that deployed-system changes feed into the documentation and the corrective-action process.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for: (a) identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) or in a substantial modification;
risks.engineering_action: Add that each rollback, its trigger, the failed check results, and the versions involved are automatically logged and linked to the audit record.

addressed_by.covers: audit records tracing model version used for each screening decision

recommendations: Define quantitative approval and rollback criteria for safety, robustness and fairness checks, and make rollback mandatory when they are breached.
Specify a fail-safe fallback during rollback and protect the approved-version registry and rollback actions with integrity and access controls.
Log every rollback event with trigger and version details and link it to the audit records and corrective-action process.

art:13:p3: full text of the Act

requirement_text: The system shall ingest candidate resumes, cover letters, and application form responses submitted through the recruitment portal.

assessment.summary: FR-1 only ingests candidate application data. None of the supplied provisions imposes a requirement-level obligation on this ingestion function, because the provisions cover notified bodies, authorities, sandboxes and registration by public deployers. Related controls such as logging, data validation and access control sit in other requirements.

requirement_text: The system shall provide candidates with a channel to request review of a decision that was influenced by automated ranking.

assessment.summary: None of the supplied provisions impose an obligation on a candidate-facing review channel. They cover GPAI model evaluation, notified bodies, Commission procedures and Annex III amendments. The appeal right in Art. 44(3) applies to decisions of notified bodies, not to candidates. No requirement-level gap can be cited from these provisions.

requirement_text: The system shall generate a suitability score for each candidate based on job requirements, experience, education, and skills extracted from the application.

assessment.summary: FR-2 defines a suitability score for candidate screening (employment, high-risk) but does not specify data governance for the training data behind it (design choices, assumptions about what skills or education proxies measure, representativeness, bias examination). It also sets no pre-defined accuracy metrics or thresholds for testing. NFR-1 to NFR-3 cover part of this, but bias examination and mitigation and representativeness remain open.

risks.description: Score is derived from education, experience and extracted skills, which can act as proxies for protected groups. The SRS requires bias measurement (NFR-2) but no examination of training data for bias, no mitigation measures and no acceptance criteria.
risks.quote: appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases identified according to point (f);
risks.engineering_action: Add a requirement to examine training data and score features for proxy bias, define mitigation measures and set acceptance thresholds for group disparity, with results documented.

addressed_by.covers: detection of performance differences across demographic groups
prevention of direct use of protected attributes as ranking inputs

risks.description: FR-2 does not state the assumptions about what job requirements, experience, education and skills represent as predictors of suitability, nor how the extracted features and labels were designed and prepared. A score built on unvalidated assumptions can be invalid or discriminatory.
risks.quote: the formulation of assumptions, in particular with respect to the information that the data are supposed to measure and represent;
risks.engineering_action: Document the design choices and the validity assumptions linking each score input to job suitability, including how skills are extracted, and the labelling basis of the training data.

addressed_by.covers: cleaning and label consistency checks (data preparation, 10(2)(c))

risks.description: Training, validation and testing data must be relevant, representative and appropriate for the job roles, geographies and applicant populations in scope. The SRS only checks missing values, duplicates and label consistency, not representativeness or the deployment context.
risks.quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose.
risks.engineering_action: Specify representativeness criteria per role, region and applicant group, and assess data gaps before training. Evaluate the score on data reflecting the deployment setting (Art. 10(4)).

addressed_by.covers: error, completeness and duplicate checks on datasets

risks.description: No accuracy or validity metrics and no pre-defined thresholds are declared for the suitability score, so testing has no acceptance criteria. NFR-5 alerts refer to 'configured thresholds' that are never defined.
risks.quote: Testing shall be carried out against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Define metrics (e.g. rank correlation with validated outcomes, error rates) and pass/fail thresholds for the score, and require testing against them before release.

addressed_by.covers: alerts when accuracy or bias metrics fall outside configured thresholds

recommendations: Add bias examination of training data and score features, with mitigation measures and acceptance thresholds.
Document the design choices and assumptions that link score inputs to job suitability, and how data was labelled and prepared.
Define representativeness and deployment-context criteria for training, validation and testing data.
Declare accuracy and validity metrics and pre-defined thresholds for testing the suitability score before release.

art:13:p3: vector similarity to the requirement

requirement_text: The system shall rank candidates for recruiter review using the generated suitability score.

assessment.summary: FR-3 ranks candidates by suitability score, a high-risk recruitment use, but states no accuracy or validation metrics for the ranking. Most controls (override, logging, explanation, bias measurement) exist elsewhere in the SRS; the remaining gap is predefined testing thresholds for the ranking itself.

risks.description: Ranking output has no predefined performance metrics or acceptance thresholds to test against before deployment; NFR-2 measures group performance and NFR-5 alerts on thresholds, but neither defines pre-deployment test criteria for ranking quality.
risks.quote: Testing shall be carried out against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Define ranking-specific metrics (e.g., rank correlation, top-k precision, per-group parity) with pass/fail thresholds, and require testing against them before release and after each model change.

addressed_by.covers: performance measured separately across demographic groups
alerts when accuracy or bias metrics fall outside configured thresholds

risks.description: Ranking is built on datasets whose representativeness for the applicant population is not required; NFR-1 checks only missing values, duplicates, and label consistency.
risks.quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose.
risks.engineering_action: Add representativeness and statistical-property checks of training and validation data against the intended applicant population (roles, groups) and document the results.

addressed_by.covers: validation of datasets for missing values, duplicates, and inconsistent labels (errors and completeness)

recommendations: Define ranking-specific test metrics and acceptance thresholds, and gate release on them.
Add dataset representativeness and statistical-property checks for the applicant population.

requirement_text: The system shall explain the main factors that influenced each candidate suitability score in language understandable to a recruiter.

assessment.summary: FR-4 gives recruiters an explanation of the main score factors, which supports Art. 13 transparency. It does not specify accuracy, limitations or fidelity of the explanations, and it does not cover the affected candidate's right to an explanation, so candidates could be denied a meaningful account of the AI's role in decisions about them.

risks.description: FR-4 directs explanations only to recruiters; nothing provides affected candidates with a clear and meaningful explanation of the AI system's role in a decision and the main elements of that decision.
risks.quote: shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken.
risks.engineering_action: Extend FR-4 or add a requirement to produce a candidate-facing explanation of the AI's role and the main decision elements, deliverable on request and linked to the FR-10 review channel.

addressed_by.covers: channel for candidates to request review of a decision influenced by automated ranking

risks.description: FR-4 does not require that explanations faithfully reflect the model's actual behaviour or state their limitations and confidence, so recruiters may misinterpret scores and over-rely on them.
risks.quote: operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system’s output and use it appropriately
risks.engineering_action: Specify that explanations are derived from the model's actual feature contributions, include limitations and uncertainty, and are validated for fidelity and recruiter comprehension in testing.

addressed_by.covers: tells recruiters that a ranking was generated by an automated decision-support model, supporting appropriate use of the output

risks.description: The requirement does not call for recruiter training on interpreting the explanations and scores, so 'understandable to a recruiter' is unverified.
risks.quote: shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf
risks.engineering_action: Add onboarding material and in-product guidance on reading the explanations, and run usability testing with recruiters to confirm understandability.

recommendations: Add a candidate-facing explanation of the AI's role and the main decision elements, linked to the FR-10 review channel.
Require explanations to be faithful to the model and to state limitations and uncertainty, and validate them with recruiter usability testing.
Provide recruiter AI-literacy guidance on interpreting scores and explanations.

requirement_text: The system shall notify recruiters when a candidate ranking was generated by an automated decision-support model.

assessment.summary: FR-5 tells recruiters that a ranking came from an automated model. None of the supplied provisions imposes a requirement-level obligation on this function. The provisions cover notifying authorities, notified bodies, certificates, GPAI model notification and deployer log retention, so they do not apply to this requirement.

requirement_text: The system shall allow a human recruiter to review, override, or reject any automated ranking before a candidate is removed from consideration.

assessment.summary: FR-6 supplies the core override/reject capability for recruiters, but it only covers the removal decision. It does not support automation-bias awareness or a stop/interrupt function, and it does not require that the oversight users be competent and trained.

risks.description: FR-6 lets recruiters override rankings but has no measure to make them aware of automation bias or to stop over-reliance on the score. For example, it does not require showing score limitations, or requiring a documented rationale when a recruiter accepts a ranking that removes a candidate.
risks.quote: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
risks.engineering_action: Add UI and workflow safeguards against automation bias: display score limitations and uncertainty, and require a confirmation or rationale before a ranking-driven removal is finalised. Include these in the recruiter guidance.

addressed_by.covers: notifies recruiters that the ranking is generated by an automated decision-support model (supports awareness under 14(4)(b))
explains main score factors so recruiters can interpret the output (14(4)(c))

risks.description: The requirement covers review, override and rejection of rankings per candidate. It does not give oversight users a way to halt or suspend automated ranking, for example when anomalies are detected.
risks.quote: to intervene in the operation of the high-risk AI system or interrupt the system through a ‘stop’ button or a similar procedure that allows the system to come to a halt in a safe state.
risks.engineering_action: Add a recruiter or admin control to pause automated scoring and ranking, with a safe fallback to manual screening. Tie it to the anomaly alerts.

addressed_by.covers: rollback to a previously approved model version when checks fail (a partial intervention mechanism)

risks.description: FR-6 does not say that review is limited to assigned recruiters with the competence, training and authority to override. It also does not say that the override is applied before removal in every pathway, such as bulk or auto-reject.
risks.quote: Deployers shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support.
risks.engineering_action: State in FR-6 that the override role is restricted to trained, authorised reviewers. Block any removal path, including bulk actions, that bypasses recruiter review.

addressed_by.covers: restricts access to candidate data and explanations to authorised recruitment staff

recommendations: Add automation-bias safeguards (limitations display, confirmation or rationale before ranking-driven removal).
Provide a pause/stop control for automated ranking with a manual-screening fallback.
Restrict override to trained, authorised reviewers and prevent any removal path that bypasses review.

requirement_text: The system shall log every model-generated score, ranking, explanation, recruiter override, and final screening decision.

assessment.summary: FR-7 lists what to log (scores, rankings, explanations, overrides, decisions) but sets no retention period and does not log risk-relevant system events such as errors, threshold breaches or model changes. Without these, logs may not support traceability, post-market monitoring or deployer log-keeping duties.

risks.description: No retention period is set for the logs, and no requirement in the SRS sets one, so logs could be deleted before the minimum of at least six months.
risks.quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
risks.engineering_action: Add a log retention requirement (at least six months, longer if justified by the intended purpose). Reconcile it with GDPR data-minimisation limits and make it configurable for deployers (Art. 26(6)).

risks.description: Logging is limited to outputs and human actions. It does not record events that identify risk situations or substantial modifications (model version changes, processing errors, out-of-threshold conditions) or feed post-market monitoring.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for: (a) identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk
risks.engineering_action: Extend FR-7 to log system events: model version and deployment changes, input-validation failures, errors, and threshold breaches raised by NFR-5. Make these logs available to the post-market monitoring process and deployer monitoring.

addressed_by.covers: traceability of input data, model version and human actions per screening decision (12(2) traceability)

recommendations: Specify a minimum log retention period of at least six months, with a deployer-configurable setting and a data-protection review.
Add system-level event logging (errors, model changes, threshold breaches) that supports risk identification and post-market monitoring.

requirement_text: The system shall retain audit records for each screening decision so that reviewers can trace the input data, model version, and human actions involved.

assessment.summary: FR-8 retains audit records for tracing input, model version and human actions, but states no retention period, no logging of risk or substantial-modification events, and no identification of the reviewing persons. FR-7 covers part of the logging, but no requirement sets the retention period or integrity protection of the records.

risks.description: No retention period is specified for the audit records, so they could be deleted before the minimum of six months, or before the period appropriate to the intended purpose.
risks.quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
risks.engineering_action: Add a configurable retention period of at least six months, justified for the recruitment purpose and aligned with data protection law. Enforce it with automated retention and deletion controls.

risks.description: The records cover decision tracing only. They do not require logging of events relevant to identifying risk or substantial-modification situations, supporting post-market monitoring, or deployer operational monitoring, such as model version changes, rollbacks, threshold alerts and drift.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for:
risks.engineering_action: Extend the audit record scope to model deployment and rollback events, monitoring threshold breaches, and anomalies relevant to risk, post-market monitoring and deployer monitoring.

addressed_by.covers: automatic logging of scores, rankings, explanations, overrides and final decisions (12(1))

risks.description: The requirement says only 'human actions' and does not require that audit records identify the reviewer, the use period, or reviewer access to the records. It also has no tamper-evidence or integrity protection for the stored records.
risks.quote: shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.
risks.engineering_action: Specify that each record includes the reviewer identity, timestamp, model version and input reference. Make the logs append-only or tamper-evident, with access limited under NFR-4.

addressed_by.covers: automatic logging of recruiter overrides and final decisions
access control on candidate data and explanations

recommendations: Add a retention period of at least six months, justified for the recruitment purpose and aligned with data protection law.
Extend the logged events to model changes, rollbacks, monitoring breaches and anomalies relevant to risk and post-market monitoring.
Record the reviewer identity and use timestamps, and make the audit store tamper-evident with controlled access.

requirement_text: The system shall prevent the use of facial recognition, biometric identification, or emotion recognition during candidate screening.

assessment.summary: FR-9 is a protective control that blocks facial recognition, biometric identification and emotion recognition in candidate screening, which supports Art. 5(1)(f) and (g). The remaining gaps are that the wording is not clearly tied to the Art. 3 definitions and that no mechanism or evidence shows the block is enforced.

risks.description: "Prevent" is vague and covers neither biometric categorisation (e.g. inferring race or beliefs from facial data) nor inference of emotions or intentions from voice or video in interviews, so prohibited practices could still enter screening.
risks.quote: the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions
risks.engineering_action: Reword FR-9 to name the Art. 3 terms (biometric data, identification, categorisation, emotion recognition) and to cover inference from any biometric input (face, voice, video). Define the technical enforcement point, such as input-type blocking and a feature allowlist, and add tests showing that biometric inputs are rejected.

addressed_by.covers: excludes protected attributes such as race, religion and political opinion as ranking inputs, which partly limits the inference of categories in Art. 5(1)(g)

risks.description: FR-1 allows only text-based inputs, but nothing says FR-9 is enforced against uploaded photos, video or audio, or monitored for the model inferring biometric traits, so enforcement cannot be shown.
risks.quote: the use of biometric categorisation systems that categorise individually natural persons based on their biometric data to deduce or infer their race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation
risks.engineering_action: Add an input-validation rule that strips or rejects image, audio and video data in the portal. Log blocked attempts and add a release check confirming that no biometric features are used by the scoring model.

addressed_by.covers: logs every model-generated score, ranking and explanation, which can evidence what the model produced

recommendations: Reword FR-9 to use the Art. 3 definitions, extend it to biometric categorisation and to emotion or intention inference, and specify how it is technically enforced.
Reject biometric media at ingestion, log blocked attempts, and add a release test that no biometric features reach the scoring model.

requirement_text: The system must validate training and evaluation datasets for missing values, duplicate records, and inconsistent labels before model training.

assessment.summary: NFR-1 covers basic data-quality checks (missing values, duplicates, label inconsistency) but not the wider Article 10 governance practices: provenance, representativeness, bias examination and documented data-preparation. A recruitment scoring system could therefore train on unrepresentative or biased data without detection.

risks.description: The requirement checks only technical data quality; it has no bias examination or mitigation of training/validation/test data before training, and no acceptance criteria for the validation outcome.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Extend pre-training validation with a bias examination of the datasets (label and outcome skew across groups, proxy features) plus documented mitigation steps and pass/fail criteria that gate model training.

addressed_by.covers: measurement of model performance across demographic groups (partial bias detection, on the trained model rather than the data sets)
exclusion of protected attributes as ranking inputs

risks.description: The requirement does not require checks that datasets are relevant, representative and have appropriate statistical properties for the candidate populations and job contexts. It also does not define how completeness or error thresholds are judged.
risks.quote: shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose
risks.engineering_action: Add representativeness and statistical-property checks (distribution by job family, region and group) and define acceptance thresholds for missing, duplicate and inconsistent records.

risks.description: Validation results, data origin, labelling and cleaning operations and identified data gaps are not required to be recorded, so data governance cannot be evidenced for conformity assessment.
risks.quote: relevant data-preparation processing operations, such as annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment and aggregation;
risks.engineering_action: Require each validation run to produce a versioned report covering data source, cleaning/labelling operations applied, issues found, remediation, and unresolved data gaps, retained with the technical documentation.

recommendations: Add dataset-level bias examination and mitigation, with gating criteria, to the pre-training validation.
Add representativeness and statistical-property checks and explicit acceptance thresholds for data errors and completeness.
Generate and retain versioned data-validation reports documenting data origin, preparation operations and identified gaps.

requirement_text: The system must measure model performance separately across demographic groups where lawful demographic evaluation data is available.

assessment.summary: NFR-2 measures performance per demographic group, which supports bias examination, but it sets no acceptance criteria or mitigation, and its 'where lawful data is available' qualifier lets evaluation be skipped. It also does not specify the safeguards for any special-category data used to do the evaluation.

risks.description: Per-group measurement has no acceptance thresholds, bias-mitigation step or documented follow-up. NFR-5 alerts on bias metrics, but nothing requires acting on disparities found in NFR-2 measurements.
risks.quote: appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases identified according to point (f);
risks.engineering_action: Define fairness metrics and acceptance thresholds per group. Require documented mitigation (re-sampling, re-weighting, retraining) and a release gate when thresholds are breached.

addressed_by.covers: detection of bias metrics falling outside configured thresholds (detect part of 10(2)(g))
rollback of a model that fails fairness checks

risks.description: The 'where lawful demographic evaluation data is available' qualifier lets the system skip group evaluation entirely. No requirement assesses data availability or representativeness for the groups affected, or records the gaps.
risks.quote: They shall have the appropriate statistical properties, including, where applicable, as regards the persons or groups of persons in relation to whom the high-risk AI system is intended to be used.
risks.engineering_action: Require a documented assessment of group coverage and sample sizes in the test data. Where demographic data is unavailable, require a fallback (proxy analysis, synthetic or anonymised data, targeted collection) and record the data gap and its remediation.

addressed_by.covers: data quality checks on missing values, duplicates and label inconsistencies (completeness and error-freeness aspects of 10(3))

risks.description: Using demographic data (which may be special-category data) for bias evaluation is not tied to the strict-necessity conditions and safeguards. These include pseudonymisation, access controls, no third-party transfer, deletion after use and records of why the processing was necessary.
risks.quote: the providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons.
risks.engineering_action: Add acceptance criteria that demographic evaluation data is processed only when strictly necessary. It should be pseudonymised, access-restricted, not transferred, deleted after bias correction or at end of retention, and its necessity documented in processing records.

addressed_by.covers: access restricted to authorised recruitment staff for candidate data (partial coverage of 10(5)(c))

recommendations: Define per-group fairness metrics, thresholds, mitigation steps and a release gate tied to NFR-2 results.
Require a documented assessment of group coverage and a fallback evaluation approach when demographic data is unavailable.
Specify Article 10(5) safeguards (pseudonymisation, restricted access, no transfer, deletion, necessity record) for demographic evaluation data.

requirement_text: The system must not use protected attributes such as race, religion, disability, or political opinion as ranking inputs.

assessment.summary: NFR-3 excludes protected attributes as direct ranking inputs, which is a useful control. It does not address proxy features, bias mitigation in the data or the lawful handling of special-category data for bias testing, so indirect discrimination could remain.

risks.description: Excluding protected attributes only as direct ranking inputs does not address proxy variables (e.g. names, postcodes, employment gaps, university) that can reproduce discriminatory outcomes. There is also no stated bias mitigation or acceptance criteria for the training data.
risks.quote: appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases identified according to point (f)
risks.engineering_action: Extend NFR-3 to cover proxy features: run proxy and correlation analysis on features, exclude or constrain proxies, and set documented bias acceptance thresholds. Re-test on every retraining.

addressed_by.covers: examination/measurement of model performance across demographic groups (detection part of 10(2)(f))
alerts when bias metrics fall outside configured thresholds

risks.description: The requirement does not state how special-category data (race, religion, disability, political opinion) will be handled if it is needed for bias detection. Excluding it from ranking inputs could conflict with NFR-2's demographic evaluation unless the Article 10(5) conditions and safeguards are specified.
risks.quote: the providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons
risks.engineering_action: Clarify that protected attributes are held only in a segregated evaluation store, used only for bias detection and correction, never fed to the ranking model, access-controlled, and deleted per Article 10(5)(e). Document why other data is insufficient.

addressed_by.covers: access controls limiting who can view candidate data (10(5)(c) access restriction)

recommendations: Extend NFR-3 to proxy-feature detection and mitigation, with documented bias acceptance thresholds checked at each retraining.
Specify segregated, access-controlled handling of protected attributes used only for bias evaluation, with deletion rules aligned to Article 10(5).

requirement_text: The system must maintain access controls so that only authorised recruitment staff can view candidate data and model explanations.

assessment.summary: NFR-4 is an access-control requirement for candidate data and explanations. The supplied provisions are mostly authority, procedural and market-surveillance rules and impose no requirement-level obligation on it, so no gap is raised.

requirement_text: The system must produce monitoring alerts when model accuracy, bias metrics, or data quality checks fall outside configured thresholds.

assessment.summary: NFR-5 provides threshold alerts for accuracy, bias and data quality, which is a useful monitoring control. It does not state that the data is systematically collected, documented and analysed under a documented post-market monitoring plan, so continuous compliance evaluation is not shown.

risks.description: Threshold alerts are not a documented post-market monitoring system or plan. The requirement does not say that performance data is actively and systematically collected, documented and analysed over the system's lifetime, or that this is used to evaluate continuous compliance.
risks.quote: The post-market monitoring system shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data which may be provided by deployers or which may be collected through other sources on the performance of high-risk AI systems throughout their lifetime
risks.engineering_action: Add a requirement for a documented post-market monitoring plan, included in the Annex IV technical documentation. It should define the data sources (including deployer feedback), the metrics, the review cadence and the compliance evaluation, with alerts as one input.

addressed_by.covers: records of model scores, rankings, explanations, overrides and decisions, which are performance data inputs to monitoring
audit records tracing input data, model version and human actions

risks.description: Alert thresholds are only 'configured'. No requirement says they are defined in advance, justified for the intended purpose, or documented, and nothing sets out what response follows a breach.
risks.quote: Testing shall be carried out against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Require that the metrics and thresholds be predefined and justified for the hiring use case, with documented owners and a response procedure for each breach. The procedure should include escalation and the NFR-6 rollback.

addressed_by.covers: per-group performance measurement that supplies the bias metrics

risks.description: Alerts do not record threshold breaches or alert handling. This weakens traceability of events that could indicate risk or support post-market monitoring.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for: (a) identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk
risks.engineering_action: Log every alert with the metric, threshold, value, timestamp and model version. Also log the acknowledgement and the corrective action taken.

recommendations: Add a documented post-market monitoring plan covering data collection, analysis and the evaluation of continuous compliance.
Define and justify the thresholds in advance, and tie each alert to an owner and a response, including rollback.
Log all alerts and their handling as monitoring evidence.

requirement_text: The system should support rollback to a previously approved model version if a deployed model fails safety, robustness, or fairness checks.

assessment.summary: NFR-6 provides rollback to an approved model version, which is a sound fail-safe control. However, it does not define who triggers rollback, which thresholds apply, or how a rollback is documented and communicated, and it does not tie rollback to the corrective-action duties for non-conforming systems.

risks.description: Rollback is triggered by failing 'safety, robustness, or fairness checks' with no defined metrics, thresholds or acceptance criteria, and no link to NFR-5 alerts. The trigger is therefore ambiguous and the fail-safe may not activate.
risks.quote: Testing shall be carried out against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: Define the rollback trigger criteria (metrics, thresholds, who may authorise) and link them to the NFR-5 alert thresholds. Also define how the 'previously approved' version is designated and validated.

addressed_by.covers: configured thresholds on accuracy, bias and data quality that can signal a failing model

risks.description: Rollback is only a technical capability. It does not require that a rollback, or the non-conformity that caused it, leads to documented corrective action or to informing deployers, distributors or authorities.
risks.quote: shall immediately take the necessary corrective actions to bring that system into conformity, to withdraw it, to disable it, or to recall it, as appropriate.
risks.engineering_action: Add a rollback procedure that records the cause and the version restored, and notifies deployers. It should trigger a corrective-action and escalation workflow in the provider's processes.

risks.description: The requirement does not state that rollback events and the reverted model version are recorded, or that rollback targets stay within the validated scope of the technical documentation. Traceability and the assessment of whether a change is substantial are therefore weakened.
risks.quote: shall undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification
risks.engineering_action: Require that each rollback or version change is versioned and logged. Rollback targets should be limited to versions covered by the existing conformity assessment and technical documentation, and any change outside that scope should be evaluated as a possible substantial modification.

addressed_by.covers: audit records tracing the model version used for each screening decision

recommendations: Define rollback trigger metrics, thresholds and approval authority, linked to NFR-5 alerts.
Integrate rollback with a corrective-action and deployer notification workflow.
Log rollback events and restrict targets to versions covered by the existing conformity assessment and technical documentation.
